input: Track my net worth monthly in a spreadsheet

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The types of assets and liabilities included (e.g. cash, investments, property, loans, credit cards) determine how many rows and categories the spreadsheet needs.
Whether this tracks one person or a household/couple changes how accounts are grouped and labelled.
The spreadsheet tool being used (Excel, Google Sheets, Apple Numbers, etc.) determines formulas, sharing options, and available features.
How far back they want historical data to go affects how much past data entry work is required upfront.
Whether they want charts and visual dashboards vs. a simple table changes the design complexity significantly.
The primary goal — spotting trends, hitting a savings target, preparing for a financial review — shapes which metrics and summaries to highlight.
Whether they want a ready-made template to fill in or step-by-step guidance to build it themselves determines the format of the output.

gold.taskTitle: Build a monthly net worth tracking spreadsheet
gold.taskDescription: Set up a spreadsheet to record and monitor net worth on a monthly basis, capturing assets and liabilities over time.

questions.title: Which asset and liability types do you need to track?
questions.description: Identify the specific categories to include, such as checking/savings accounts, investment portfolios, real estate, car loans, student debt, credit card balances, etc.

questions.title: Is this for you alone or a shared household?
questions.description: Determine whether the spreadsheet should track one individual's finances or combine figures for a couple or family.

questions.title: Which spreadsheet tool are you using — Excel, Google Sheets, other?
questions.description: Confirm the platform so the design, formulas, and sharing setup can be tailored to it.

questions.title: How many months of past data do you want to enter upfront?
questions.description: Establish whether the tracker starts fresh from this month or needs columns/rows for historical months to show a baseline trend.

questions.title: Do you want charts and a visual dashboard, or just a clean data table?
questions.description: Decide on the level of visual complexity — a simple row-by-row log versus an automatic chart showing net worth growth over time.

questions.title: What is the main thing you want this tracker to help you achieve?
questions.description: Clarify the primary goal — for example, reaching a savings milestone, monitoring debt paydown, preparing for retirement planning, or simply staying aware of financial health.

questions.title: Do you want a ready-made template or instructions to build it yourself?
questions.description: Determine whether to deliver a fully structured spreadsheet template to fill in, or a step-by-step guide for building it from scratch.
